builtins.name: adsr
builtins.doc: Gated ADSR envelope. Rises while the gate is positive, releases when it returns to zero. Times are in seconds; sustain is a level in 0..=1.

builtins.name: afollow
builtins.doc: Asymmetric parameter follower. Smooths rising segments over `attack` and falling ones over `release` (halfway response times, in seconds).

builtins.name: allpass
builtins.doc: Allpass filter. Passes all frequencies but shifts their phase around the center frequency.

builtins.name: allpole
builtins.doc: First-order allpass filter with a configurable delay at DC, in samples (must be > 0).

builtins.name: bandpass
builtins.doc: Bandpass filter. Keeps frequencies near the center, attenuating either side.

builtins.name: bandrez
builtins.doc: Resonant two-pole bandpass filter.

builtins.name: bell
builtins.doc: Bell equalizer. Boosts or cuts a band around the center frequency by `gain` (an amplitude multiplier, not dB).

builtins.name: biquad
builtins.doc: Arbitrary biquad filter with coefficients in normalized form. All five coefficients must be constants.

builtins.name: brown
builtins.doc: Brown noise: -6 dB per octave. Darker than pink.

builtins.name: butterpass
builtins.doc: Second-order Butterworth lowpass. Maximally flat passband, no resonance control.

builtins.name: chorus
builtins.doc: Five-voice mono chorus, mixed with the dry signal. Stack two with different seeds for stereo. All parameters except the audio input are constants.

builtins.name: clip
builtins.doc: Hard-clip the signal to -1..=1.

builtins.name: clip_to
builtins.doc: Hard-clip the signal to `minimum`..=`maximum`. Both bounds are constants.

builtins.name: dcblock
builtins.doc: Remove DC offset, keeping the signal zero-centered. Cutoff is 10 Hz.

builtins.name: declick
builtins.doc: Fade the signal in over 10 ms from time zero, suppressing the click at the start of a graph.

builtins.name: delay
builtins.doc: Fixed delay of `time` seconds, rounded to the nearest sample. The time is a constant — use `tap` for a modulatable delay.

builtins.name: dsf_saw
builtins.doc: Saw-like discrete summation formula oscillator. `roughness` in 0..=1 sets how much successive partials are attenuated.

builtins.name: env
builtins.doc: Time-based ADSR for one-shot voices. Attack, decay and sustain fill `duration`. The note is held for `duration` and the voice lasts `duration + release`. All arguments are constants.

builtins.name: dsf_square
builtins.doc: Square-like discrete summation formula oscillator. `roughness` in 0..=1 sets how much successive partials are attenuated.

builtins.name: fir3
builtins.doc: Three-point symmetric FIR filter, specified by its `gain` (>= 0) at the Nyquist frequency. A gain below 1 gives a gentle lowpass.

builtins.name: follow
builtins.doc: Parameter follower. Smooths the signal with the given halfway response time, in seconds.

builtins.name: hammond
builtins.doc: Hammond organ wavetable oscillator. Emphasizes the first three partials.

builtins.name: highpass
builtins.doc: Resonant highpass filter.

builtins.name: highpole
builtins.doc: First-order one-pole one-zero highpass. No resonance.

builtins.name: highshelf
builtins.doc: High shelf filter. Scales everything above the center frequency by `gain` (an amplitude multiplier).

builtins.name: hold
builtins.doc: Sample-and-hold. Samples the signal at `frequency` Hz; `variability` in 0..=1 jitters the sampling interval and is a constant.

builtins.name: impulse
builtins.doc: A single one followed by silence. Useful for exciting `pluck` or measuring an impulse response.

builtins.name: input
builtins.doc: One channel of the live audio input, counted from 0. Silence until an input device is chosen in the settings panel, and on any channel the chosen device does not have — so a piece written against an interface still runs on the laptop it is edited on.

builtins.name: limiter
builtins.doc: Look-ahead limiter holding the signal to -1..=1. Look-ahead equals the attack time. Times are constants, in seconds.

builtins.name: line
builtins.doc: One straight segment: `start` to `end` over `duration` seconds, held constant at `end` value after `duration`.

builtins.name: lorenz
builtins.doc: Lorenz chaotic oscillator. The frequency input has only a slight effect on the output.

builtins.name: lowpass
builtins.doc: Resonant lowpass filter.

builtins.name: lowpole
builtins.doc: First-order one-pole lowpass. No resonance.

builtins.name: lowrez
builtins.doc: Resonant two-pole lowpass filter.

builtins.name: lowshelf
builtins.doc: Low shelf filter. Scales everything below the center frequency by `gain` (an amplitude multiplier).

builtins.name: mls
builtins.doc: Maximum length sequence noise: a repeating pseudorandom run of -1 and 1.

builtins.name: mls_bits
builtins.doc: Maximum length sequence noise from an n-bit sequence (1..=31). More bits means a longer period before it repeats. Constant.

builtins.name: moog
builtins.doc: Moog-style resonant lowpass ladder filter.

builtins.name: morph
builtins.doc: Filter that morphs continuously between modes: `morph` runs -1 (lowpass) to 0 (peak) to 1 (highpass).

builtins.name: noise
builtins.doc: White noise.

builtins.name: notch
builtins.doc: Notch filter. Removes a narrow band around the center frequency.

builtins.name: organ
builtins.doc: Organ wavetable oscillator. Emphasizes octave partials.

builtins.name: peak
builtins.doc: Peaking filter.

builtins.name: perc
builtins.doc: Self-contained percussive envelope: rise, fall, silence. Both times are constants.

builtins.name: pink
builtins.doc: Pink noise: -3 dB per octave.

builtins.name: pinkpass
builtins.doc: Pinking filter: -3 dB per octave. Turns white noise into pink.

builtins.name: pluck
builtins.doc: Karplus-Strong plucked string. Feed it a burst — `impulse()` or a short noise envelope — as the excitation. Frequency, gain and damping (0..=1) are constants.

builtins.name: poly_pulse
builtins.doc: PolyBLEP pulse wave. Fast and fairly bandlimited; `width` in 0..=1 is the duty cycle.

builtins.name: poly_saw
builtins.doc: PolyBLEP saw wave. Fast and fairly bandlimited.

builtins.name: poly_square
builtins.doc: PolyBLEP square wave. Fast and fairly bandlimited.

builtins.name: pulse
builtins.doc: Bandlimited pulse wave oscillator. `width` in 0..=1 is the duty cycle.

builtins.name: ramp
builtins.doc: Rising ramp from 0 to 1 at the given repetition frequency, starting at 0. Not bandlimited — useful as a phasor, not as audio.

builtins.name: resonator
builtins.doc: Constant-gain bandpass resonator.

builtins.name: reverb
builtins.doc: Reverb (32-channel FDN). `room_size` is in meters (10 is an average room), `time` is the decay to -60 dB in seconds, `damping` in 0..=1 rolls off the highs. Wet only: `x + reverb(x, 10, 3, 0.5) * 0.2`. All parameters except the audio input are constants.

builtins.name: reverb2
builtins.doc: Hybrid FDN reverb — richer and more expensive than `reverb`. `room_size` is in meters and clamps to 10..=30, `diffusion` in 0..=1 thickens the tail, `modulation` around 1 adds movement (higher goes audibly Doppler), and `damping_cutoff` is the lowpass applied to each loop pass, in hertz. Wet only. All parameters except the audio input are constants.

builtins.name: reverb3
builtins.doc: Allpass-loop reverb, with no room size — just `time` to -60 dB, `diffusion` in 0..=1, and a `damping_cutoff` in hertz applied to each loop pass. Wet only. All parameters except the audio input are constants.

builtins.name: reverb4
builtins.doc: Reverb with a slow fade-in, for swells rather than rooms. `room_size` is in meters and is treated as at least 15; below that the delay times stop sounding like a space. Wet only. Both `room_size` and `time` are constants.

builtins.name: rossler
builtins.doc: Rossler chaotic oscillator, with peaks at multiples of the frequency input.

builtins.name: saw
builtins.doc: Bandlimited saw wavetable oscillator.

builtins.name: sin
builtins.doc: Sine oscillator.

builtins.name: soft_saw
builtins.doc: Soft saw wavetable oscillator. Contains all partials but falls off like a triangle wave.

builtins.name: square
builtins.doc: Bandlimited square wavetable oscillator.

builtins.name: tap
builtins.doc: Tapped delay line with cubic interpolation. Unlike `delay`, the delay time is a signal, so it can be modulated. It must stay within the constant `min_delay`..=`max_delay` bounds, in seconds.

builtins.name: tick
builtins.doc: Single-sample delay. The building block for feedback and comb filters.

builtins.name: triangle
builtins.doc: Bandlimited triangle wavetable oscillator.

builtins.name: list
builtins.doc: Marks numbers as one value rather than a sequence. A lane is read by note — the nth note takes the nth value, wrapping — so `div: [2, 3]` gives the first note 2 and the second 3, where `div: list(2, 3)` gives every note both. `'[2, 3]` is the same value written short. Only a lane reads one.

builtins.name: len
builtins.doc: The number of elements in the list.

builtins.name: zip
builtins.doc: Pair elements positionally: `zip([1, 2], [3, 4])` is `[[1, 3], [2, 4]]`. Every argument must be a list and all must be the same length.

builtins.name: stack
builtins.doc: Creates patterns that sound at once instead of in turn: `stack([c4;2, e4;2], [g4;4])`. Each argument keeps its own division, so the layers need not agree on a rhythm. Creates chords and polyphony.

builtins.name: rev
builtins.doc: Reverse a list

builtins.name: palindrome
builtins.doc: The list followed by its mirror: `[a, b, c]` becomes `[a, b, c, c, b, a]`.

builtins.name: rotl
builtins.doc: Rotate left, wrapping. `amount` defaults to 1; a negative amount rotates right.

builtins.name: rotr
builtins.doc: Rotate right, wrapping. `amount` defaults to 1; a negative amount rotates left.

builtins.name: push
builtins.doc: A new list with `value` appended.

builtins.name: pop
builtins.doc: A new list without its last element.

builtins.name: sort
builtins.doc: The list sorted ascending.

builtins.name: sum
builtins.doc: Add every element together.

builtins.name: split
builtins.doc: Break the list into chunks of `size`.

builtins.name: choice
builtins.doc: One element picked at random. Re-rolled on every eval.

builtins.name: wchoice
builtins.doc: Weighted random choice The two lists run in parallel; weights must be finite and >= 0.

builtins.name: scramble
builtins.doc: The list shuffled. Re-rolled on every eval.

builtins.name: map
builtins.doc: Apply a function to every element: `riff.map(up)`.

builtins.name: dot
builtins.doc: Dot a written note value: `q.dot` is a dotted quarter, a quarter and an eighth. `dots` defaults to 1; `q.dot(2)` is the doubly-dotted quarter. Can be chained as well `q.dot.dot`.

builtins.name: filter
builtins.doc: Filter a list based on the predicate.

builtins.name: m2h
builtins.doc: MIDI note number to frequency in hertz: `69.m2h` is 440. Equal temperament.

builtins.name: h2m
builtins.doc: Frequency in hertz to MIDI note number, the inverse of `m2h`: `440.h2m` is 69. The result may be fractional.

builtins.name: db
builtins.doc: Decibels to a linear amplitude: `0.db` is 1, `-6.db` is about 0.5.

builtins.name: amp
builtins.doc: Linear amplitude to decibels, the inverse of `db`: `1.amp` is 0. The amplitude must be above zero.

builtins.name: cents
builtins.doc: Detune a frequency by cents, 1/100 of a semitone: `440.cents(-14)` flattens A4 slightly.

builtins.name: bpm
builtins.doc: Beats per minute to bars per second.

builtins.name: oct
builtins.doc: Transpose a MIDI note by whole octaves: `60.oct(-1)` is 48. A list is transposed note by note, keeping each one's `;` length and leaving rests alone — `[c4;q, ef, g].oct(-1)`. Nested lists move with it, so a subdivision group transposes as a group.

builtins.name: semi
builtins.doc: Transpose a MIDI note by semitones: `60.semi(7)` is 67. A list is transposed note by note, keeping each one's `;` length and leaving rests alone — `[c4;q, ef, g].semi(7)`. Nested lists move with it, so a subdivision group transposes as a group.

builtins.name: scale
builtins.doc: Snap a MIDI note to the nearest tone of a scale, given as semitone offsets within an octave: `61.scale([0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11])` is 60. A list is snapped note by note, keeping each one's `;` length and leaving rests alone, so a whole riff can be bent into a scale at once.

builtins.name: clamp
builtins.doc: Constrain a number to `lo..=hi`.

builtins.name: norm
builtins.doc: Map 0..1 onto `lo..hi`. Values outside 0..1 extrapolate; `clamp` first if you do not want that.

builtins.name: wrap
builtins.doc: Fold a number back into `lo..hi`, wrapping around rather than clamping. Useful for modular pitch.

builtins.name: round
builtins.doc: Nearest whole number, halves away from zero.

builtins.name: floor
builtins.doc: Largest whole number at or below `x`.

builtins.name: ceil
builtins.doc: Smallest whole number at or above `x`.

builtins.name: abs
builtins.doc: Magnitude, dropping the sign.

builtins.name: pow
builtins.doc: `x` raised to a power: `2.pow(10)` is 1024.

builtins.name: sqrt
builtins.doc: Square root. `x` must not be negative.

builtins.name: log2
builtins.doc: Base-2 logarithm. `x` must be above zero.

builtins.name: rand
builtins.doc: A uniform number. `rand()` draws from 0..1; `rand(lo, hi)` — or `60.rand(72)` — draws from `lo..hi`, with `hi` excluded.

builtins.name: randi
builtins.doc: A uniform whole number in `lo..hi`, with `hi` excluded. Both bounds must be whole.

builtins.name: coin
builtins.doc: 1 or 0, `coin()` is even 50/50 probability. `coin(0.25)` is 1 one time in four.

builtins.name: seed
builtins.doc: Use a fixed seed for all random values after it is set. A voice is lowered per note and does not see a top-level seed, so a `seed` inside an instrument pins that instrument identically on every note.

builtins.name: gauss
builtins.doc: A normally distributed number: clustered around `mean`, two thirds of it within one `deviation`. Both default to the standard 0 and 1. Unbounded.

builtins.name: humanize
builtins.doc: Nudge a number off its grid: `x` plus random `amount`.

builtins.name: expo
builtins.doc: An exponentially distributed number above zero with the given `mean` (default 1).

builtins.name: tri
builtins.doc: A triangular draw over `lo..hi`, peaking at `mode`.

builtins.name: cauchy
builtins.doc: A heavy-tailed draw around `median` (default 0) with the given `spread` (default 1).

builtins.name: pareto
builtins.doc: A power-law draw at or above `scale` (default 1). A smaller `shape` (default 1) makes big values likelier.

builtins.name: poisson
builtins.doc: A whole count averaging `mean` (default 1).

builtins.name: rands
builtins.doc: A list of `count` uniform numbers, from 0..1 or from `lo..hi`.

builtins.name: randis
builtins.doc: A list of `count` whole numbers in `lo..hi`, `hi` excluded.

builtins.name: walk
builtins.doc: A random walk. `Count` numbers beginning at `start`, each drifting from the one before by up to `step` either way.

builtins.name: walki
builtins.doc: `walk` in whole steps: each move is a whole number from `-step` to `step`, so the result stays on the semitone grid. `walki(16, 60, 2)` wanders a melody around middle C. `step` must be whole.

builtins.name: choices
builtins.doc: `count` elements chosen. Does not repeat. Asking for the whole list is equivalent to `scramble`. > len is an error.

builtins.name: randscale
builtins.doc: `count` notes drawn evenly from the tones of a scale given as semitone offsets within an octave between MIDI `lo` and `hi` (60..72 by default). Unlike snapping a uniform draw with `scale`, every degree is equally likely and nothing lands outside the range: `randscale(8, [0, 3, 5, 7, 10], 48, 72)` is a pentatonic riff over two octaves.

builtins.name: then
builtins.doc: Sequence one section after another: `playn(verse, lead, 4).then(chorus)`.

builtins.name: then_after
builtins.doc: `then`, with `bars` of silence in between the previous play: `playn(verse, lead, 4).then_after(1, chorus)` leaves a bar's rest before the chorus. The gap cannot be negative.

builtins.name: then_afters
builtins.doc: `then_after`, in seconds instead of bars: `playn(verse, lead, 4).then_afters(1.5, chorus)`. The seconds are converted to bars at the tempo the program was played at, so changing the tempo afterwards stretches the gap along with the music. The gap cannot be negative.

builtins.name: then_afterd
builtins.doc: `then_after`, in a written note value instead of bars: `playn(verse, lead, 4).then_afterd(h, chorus)` leaves half a bar's rest in 4/4. Takes the values a pattern is written in — `w`, `h`, `q`, `e`, `s`, dotted with `q.dot`, added with `h + e` — and how much of a bar one is follows the time signature. A plain number is refused: write `then_after` for bars or `then_afters` for seconds.

builtins.name: overlap
builtins.doc: `then`, but the section starts `bars` *before* the first one ends. Two functions will sound together over the join: `playn(verse, lead, 8).overlap(2, chorus)`. The chain carries on from whichever of the two ends later.

builtins.name: with
builtins.doc: Run a section *alongside* the previous play in the chain: `playn(verse, lead, 4).with(drums).then(chorus)`. The pair finishes when the later of them does.

builtins.name: at
builtins.doc: Place a section at an absolute bar, counted from the origin: `at(8, chorus)`. Bars are counted from 0, so `at(8, …)` is the ninth bar

builtins.name: seq
builtins.doc: Plays plays one after another without the nesting: `seq(intro, verse, chorus, verse)`. Only plays the next when the previous pattern completes.

builtins.name: then_n
builtins.doc: Run a section n `times`. `play_once(intro, lead).then_n(verse, 4)`.

builtins.name: loop
builtins.doc: Loops the entire chain prior to its call n `times`. `playn(groove, kit, 3).then_fill(roll).loop(4)` is four bars of groove-and-fill.

builtins.name: then_each
builtins.doc: One pass of the section per element of the list, in sequence, with the element from the list passed in: `play_once(intro, lead).then_each([1, 2, 4], faster)` calls `faster(1)`, then `faster(2)`, then `faster(4)`.

builtins.name: then_fill
builtins.doc: A fill is played by the play it chains from: `playn(groove, drums, 4).then_fill([1, 1, 1, 1])`. The instrument and every lane are inherited and only the pattern is new.

builtins.name: quantize
builtins.doc: Round where a chain of plays has reached up to a multiple of `grid` bars, without touching what is already playing: `playn(pat, inst, 3, 2).quantize().then(chorus)`. `grid` defaults to 1. Useful when a section's length is not a whole number of bars.

builtins.name: wait
builtins.doc: Hold a chain open for `bars` of silence before anything follows: `playn(verse, lead, 4).wait(2).then(chorus)`. What is already playing is untouched — only the next section moves, the same way `quantize` rounds the join without shortening the notes. `.then_after(2, chorus)` says the same thing about one join; `wait` is a link in the chain, so `.loop` repeats the gap with the notes. Cannot be negative.

builtins.name: waits
builtins.doc: `wait`, in seconds instead of bars: `playn(verse, lead, 4).waits(1.5)`. The seconds are converted to bars at the tempo the program was played at, so changing the tempo afterwards stretches the gap along with the music. Cannot be negative.

builtins.name: waitd
builtins.doc: `wait`, in a written note value instead of bars: `playn(verse, lead, 4).waitd(h)` waits half a bar in 4/4. Takes the values a pattern is written in — `w`, `h`, `q`, `e`, `s`, dotted with `q.dot`, added with `h + e` — and how much of a bar one is follows the time signature. A plain number is refused: write `wait` for bars or `waits` for seconds.

builtins.name: take
builtins.doc: Interrupts a play after n number of bars, `play(riff, lead).take(8).then(chorus)`.

builtins.name: stop
builtins.doc: Stops a play.

builtins.name: wthen
builtins.doc: Weighted choice between sections each iteration: `playn(intro, lead, 2).wthen([verse, chorus], [0.7, 0.3])`. Weights are relative and need not sum to 1.

builtins.name: rthen
builtins.doc: Random choice without weighting: `playn(intro, lead, 2).rthen([verse, chorus, bridge])`. Rerolls each iteration.

builtins.name: maybe
builtins.doc: Play a section with probability `chance` (0 to 1). Maybe decides each iteration: `playn(groove, drums, 4).maybe(0.25, fill)`.

builtins.name: shuffle_then
builtins.doc: Plays every section in a randomized order: `play_once(intro, lead).shuffle_then([verse, chorus, bridge])`. It is evaluated like `scramble`.

builtins.name: play
builtins.doc: Schedule a pattern on an instrument: `pat >> play(kick)`. The instrument must name a user `fn`. `rate` defaults to 1. Any further function parameter is added as a lane — `play(bass, cut: [400, 2000])` lane's values are sampled at each note's onset. Two names are reserved and reach the note rather than the instrument: `legato:` scales its length, and `pan:` places it across the stereo field from -1 (left) through 0 (centre) to 1 (right). All children of `play` follow the same conventions.

builtins.name: play_once
builtins.doc: `play`, stopping after one pass of the pattern: `[60, 64, 67] >> play_once(stab)`.

builtins.name: playn
builtins.doc: `play`, stopping after `times` passes of the pattern: `playn([220, 330], bass, 4)`. Lanes work as they do on `play`.

builtins.name: play_all
builtins.doc: Executes all plays simultaneously. `play_all(verse, bassline).then(chorus)`.

builtins.name: accel
builtins.doc: Accelerates a play's rate `from` to `to` over `bars` bars. Holds at `to` upon completion. Use in the rate parameter of `play` — `play(riff, lead, accel(1, 2, 4))`. A `to` less than from `from` slows down — `play(riff, lead, accel(2, 1, 4))` Both rates must be above zero: at zero the pattern would stop rather than slow.

builtins.name: dur
builtins.doc: The current note's length in seconds. Passed to a function used in a `play` scoped to the function.

builtins.name: qvs
builtins.doc: The quarter note in seconds. Use with lengths: `perc(0, qvs / 2)` or `delay(qvs * 0.75)`

builtins.name: qvh
builtins.doc: The quarter note in hertz — `1 / qvs`. Use in oscillators: `sin(qvh * 2)`

builtins.name: load
builtins.doc: Read an audio file into a buffer: `let amen = load("breaks/amen.wav")`. The path is relative to the file it is written in. Any format symphonia reads: wav, mp3, flac, ogg.

builtins.name: midiin
builtins.doc: A keyboard to play, in place of a pattern: `play(midiin("keystation"), lead)`, or `midiin("keystation").play(lead)`. The device is a port's name — matched on any part of it, ignoring case — or its number in the settings panel's list. `channel` is 1-16 and defaults to every channel, which is what a keyboard on its own means. A note arrives as its MIDI note number, the same thing a pattern step carries. An instrument that declares a `vel` parameter is given the velocity, 0 to 1. A keyboard has no length, so it takes neither a rate nor `play_once`/`playn`.

builtins.name: midiclock
builtins.doc: Send the transport's clock to a port, so a synth's arps and delays line up with the part written for it: `midiclock("deluge")`. Twenty-four ticks to the quarter note, plus start and stop with the transport. The device is a port's name — matched on any part of it, ignoring case — or its number. Following somebody else's clock is the other way round and is not this: it is in the settings panel under MIDI, because whether you are the slave tonight is about the rig rather than the piece.

builtins.name: cc
builtins.doc: One controller — a knob, a wheel, a pedal — as a signal: `cc("push", 74)` is 0 to 1. `channel` is 1-16 and defaults to 1. Give a range to map it straight onto something: `cc("push", 74, 1, 200, 5000)` is a filter cutoff. Smoothed over a few milliseconds, because seven bits wired to a cutoff zippers. Zero until the controller first moves, and silent when the port is not connected.

builtins.name: bend
builtins.doc: The pitch wheel as a signal, -1 to 1 with the wheel at rest reading 0 — so `note + bend("keys", 1, -2, 2)` bends two semitones either way. Give a range to change that. Smoothed like `cc`.

builtins.name: aftertouch
builtins.doc: Channel pressure — how hard the keys are being leant on — as a signal, 0 to 1. Give a range to map it. Smoothed like `cc`. Zero on a keyboard that does not send it.

builtins.name: slider
builtins.doc: A control in the panel, named where it is used: `lowpass(saw(110), slider("cutoff", 200, 5000), 1)` draws a slider called cutoff in the controls panel and reads it at audio rate, so dragging it is heard immediately with nothing recompiled. The range defaults to 0 to 1, and a fourth number says where it starts — otherwise it starts at the bottom. The name is what labels the control and what makes it the same control after an edit, so writing one name in two places is one slider moving both. Those two places need not agree on a range: what a slider holds is a position along its travel, and each place maps it into the range written there — at halfway `slider("cutoff", 200, 5000)` reads 2600 while `slider("cutoff", 0, 1)` reads 0.5, one hand moving both across their own ends. The panel draws the range declared first. A slider keeps its position across an evaluation and forgets it when the app quits, which is why the number written here is a starting point rather than a value. Smoothed over a few milliseconds, because a drag wired straight to a cutoff zippers. Written where the language wants a compile-time number — a `;` length, a pattern step, a delay time — it is the position it stood at when the program compiled; the panel marks those, and letting go of one runs the program again.

builtins.name: toggle
builtins.doc: A switch in the panel, off or on, named where it is used: `sin(220) * toggle("mute")` draws a toggle called mute and reads it at audio rate, so flipping it is heard immediately. It is 0 or 1, which makes multiplying by it the ordinary use — a part that is in or out without a number to choose. A second argument says which end it starts at: `toggle("lead", 1)` starts on. Everything else is a `slider`: one name is one control wherever it is written, it keeps its state across an evaluation and forgets it when the app quits, and its ends are smoothed over a few milliseconds so switching something in does not click.

builtins.name: trigger
builtins.doc: A button in the panel that starts a section when pressed: `trigger("fill", fill)` draws a button called fill and plays `fill` each time it is hit. The section is a `fn` named rather than called, the same thing `.then` takes, and how long it lasts is what it says — a `play_once` or `playn` inside it is a one-shot, a plain `play` keeps going. It is lowered when the program runs, not when the button is pressed, so a press compiles nothing and can fail at nothing. A press starts the section on the next beat, and pressing again restarts it from the top. Nothing else stops: a fired section plays over what is already going, and its own notes are the only ones it decides.

builtins.name: midiout
builtins.doc: Gear to send a pattern to, in place of an instrument: `play(bass, midiout("deluge"), vel: [1, .6])`. The device is a port's name — matched on any part of it, ignoring case — or its number in the settings panel's list. `channel` is 1-16 and defaults to 1. A pattern's values are MIDI note numbers, which is what `c4`, `semi` and `scale` already count in. Lanes: `vel` is 0 to 1, `chan` overrides the channel per note, and `legato` sets how long the note is held. A port that is not connected is a warning rather than an error, so a piece written for a rack still runs on the laptop it is edited on.

builtins.name: sample
builtins.doc: Read a buffer at a position: 0 is the start, 1 is the end. Anything outside that is silence. `position` is a signal: `sample(b, ramp(1 / b.secs))` -- plays forwards, `1 - ramp(...)` backwards. `channel` defaults to 0 and wraps if the buffer has fewer.

builtins.name: slice
builtins.doc: Read a portion of a buffer, once: `slice(amen, 0, 0.25)`. `start` and `end` are between 0 and 1. `start` past `end` plays that portion backwards. `rate` defaults to 1.

builtins.name: secs
builtins.doc: Attribute on a buffer. How long a buffer is, in seconds.

builtins.name: channels
builtins.doc: How many channels a buffer has — 1 for mono, 2 for a stereo file.

durations.name: w
durations.doc: Whole note — four beats, which is one bar in 4/4 and more than one in any shorter meter.

durations.name: s
durations.doc: Sixteenth note — a quarter of a beat.

durations.name: t
durations.doc: Tuplet — play this group in the next lower power of two. Three quarters in the time of two, five eighths in the time of four. Its contents have to fill the division, and cannot already come to a plain duration.
